english: no one is obliged to do more than he can

terms.comment: A legal maxim in this shape; we have found no ancient source for its wording. The Digest has the rule in Celsus’s words (below).
Literally “there is no obligation to do impossible things”: one of the rules of law at the end of the Digest.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
